questions.ask: What is your date of birth?
What are the last four digits of the phone number we have on file for you?

hints.day_month_swapped: Could you please say the month as a word?

intents.hardship: The customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss.
intents.dispute: "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product"; a claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is also a dispute.
intents.already_paid: "I already paid": covers only a payment of this past-due amount.
intents.restructure: A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments.
intents.vague: A vague period such as "next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes".
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

lines.robot: I am Freya Bank's digital assistant.
lines.scam: You can verify this call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can only explain why I am calling after a short security check.

lines.not_talk_once: I understand, this will only take a moment.

lines.tp_booked: Thank you, we will call back on {date} at {time}.

lines.condolence: I am sorry for your loss.

lines.ask_today_multi: Can you make all of these payments today?

lines.offer_floor: I understand. The rest would stay overdue, but could you pay {amount}?

lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, I cannot record that amount.
lines.date_past: That date has already passed. Which day from today on would work for you?

lines.vague_ask: Which exact day would that be?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which day could you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: To repeat, could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest date I can accept is {date}, so I will use that date.
lines.recorded: Thank you, your promise is recorded.
lines.sms_line: You will receive a text message confirming this promise.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, I could not record the promise.
lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know. Payments can take one business day to appear.
lines.dispute_line: I understand, I will not ask you for a payment on this product.
lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear that. Would you like me to connect you with our customer support team?
lines.hardship_declined: I understand, thank you for telling me.
lines.restructure_line: I will connect you with a colleague who can discuss that with you.
lines.human_ask_help: I may be able to help you myself. Is there something I can help you with first?
lines.transfer: I will transfer you now. Please hold.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: A promise cannot be changed or cancelled on this call, but you can change it in the mobile app.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I did not catch that. Do you confirm, yes or no?
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {amount}.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I could not book the callback.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer did not go through.
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our system is not responding right now.

quotes: A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt.
A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal.
Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
rules.opening_is_attempt.derivation: The first ask (full amount today) is separate from Attempt 1 (full amount on the last business day of this week); refusing the first ask triggers attempt 1, so the opening ask is not itself attempt 1.

quotes: If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once.
Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline.
rules.too_much_floor.derivation: After 'too much' the floor becomes attempt 1 (on attempt 1's date); attempt 2 names the floor again on the deadline.

quotes: When the attempts are used up, stop.
If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
If it fails, try once more.
Offer to connect them with the customer support team.
On any transfer (restructuring, support, human) add no notes at all, before or after it.

rules.deadline_adjust.assumption: Deadlines are the n-th business day, so they are always business days; for any other computed date, the default previous_business_day applies.

quotes: First ask: "Can you make this payment today?".
First ask whether the customer can pay all of them today.
If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.

rules.opening_blocks_repeat.assumption: Not stated; the opening ask (today) and attempt 1 (last business day of the week, moved to next week when today is that day) never coincide.

rules.skipped_repeat_counts.assumption: Not stated; the late-band attempt 2 date (7th business day) is always later than attempt 1's date, so no step repeats.

products.floor_pct.assumption: The floor is the product field (minimum_payment / instalment_amount), not a percentage.

products.floor_round.assumption: No rounding stated; amounts in cents.

products.promise_scale.assumption: create_promise takes the same units as get_account.

quotes: Otherwise close as `no_promise` with the reason of the first product, in `get_account` order, whose note is not `paid`.
multi.outcome_priority.derivation: The first non-paid product in account order decides the close: no priority ranking.

quotes: If not, go through the products one by one, in the order `get_account` returned them.

event_changes.assumption: No dated code changes in the materials.

changes.assumption: No dated value changes in the materials.

assumptions: Brief B (up to three products) is the governing brief; it applies Brief A except where it replaces a rule. With one product it behaves as Brief A, except that add_note is used (Brief B rule 8 replaces 'Brief A never uses add_note').
The brief names no currency; the default 'dollars' is used.
The brief does not say how often an unclear answer to a payment question is asked again; max_unclear is left unset. The brief says a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt (non_answer_counts true).
Callback: 'today or the next business day' with no rule restricting today to business days, so business_days_only is false. 'Ask once for another time' gives max_asks 2.
The date of birth is sent as YYYY-MM-DD. A date given only as numbers is read day, month, year (date_order dmy).
Opening: Brief A says to state that the call is recorded; the line says 'We record this call.' to keep the word 'recorded' out of non-promise lines.

Ladder: attempt 1 = full amount (or the floor after 'too much') on the last business day of this week, moved to next week's when today is that day. Attempt 2 (late band only) = the floor on the deadline. The early band allows 1 attempt and the late band 2, counted per product (Brief B rule 5).

Multi-product closing: promise wins if any promise was recorded. Brief A's rule 'If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as transferred with that transfer's reason' and Brief B rule 10 make any transfer close as transferred. The built-in transfer ending covers this.
Transfer to a human uses queue 'general' (Brief A rule 42); support uses 'support'; restructuring uses 'restructuring'.
Floor names: 'minimum payment' for credit cards and 'instalment' for loans, from the field names minimum_payment and instalment_amount.
